watches.description: DESCRIPTION Sized right and subtly packed with precision and performance, the Weimar GMT is perhaps one of the most stylish dual-time timepieces around. Perfectly balanced and functionally adept each watch is fused and completed with the unmistakable DuFa design codes of watchmaking. DETAILS OVERVIEW INSTRUCTION DETAILS MOVEMENT: Swiss Quartz 3 Hands with Date and GMT CASE: Stainless Steel CASE DIAMETER (mm): 38 CASE THICKNESS (mm): 9 CASE SHAPE: Round CASE COLOUR: Stainless Steel DIAL COLOUR: White BAND: Genuine Leather Strap BAND COLOUR: Black BUCKLE: Strap Buckle BAND WIDTH (mm): 18-16 WATER RESISTANCE: 3ATM WATCH WEIGHT (g): 50 WARRANTY: 2 Years International OVERVIEW WEIMAR, HOLDS A special place in the fabric of German culture. Its intriguing paradox of culture both traditional and modern, gives perfect inspiration to the range of timepieces in this collection. / During the rule of Duke Carl August, the city emerged as the home of the German Enlightenment. It drew intellectual and cultural luminaries such as Johan Wolfgang von Goethe, Freidrich Schiller who helped establish a new humanism, from the synthesis of ideas from Romanticism and Classicism. / Other talents such as famed composer, Johann Sebastian Bach, philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche made Weimar perhaps the capital of culture in Europe at the time. / In the 20th century, the city is known as being the birthplace of the Bauhaus movement. While the movements differed vastly in aesthetics, both the era of classicism and modernity pushed the experience of human expression further creating indelible marks in history. INSTRUCTION English

Moving to Weimar in 1919 he transformed what was the Grand-Ducal Saxon School of Arts and Crafts into the famed Bauhaus academy. By attracting and mentoring a faculty that included some of the most famous names in 20th Century design, a truly groundbreaking, design philosophy was to emerge, spurred on by Gropius. / The school’s most innovative educational aspect was its dualistic approach to training in the workshops, which were codirected by a craftsman (master of works) and an artist (master of form). / Gropius himself as designer, extended his hand from furniture, interiors through to automobiles, wallpaper. As avant-garde architect his work took in a thoroughly modern approach as was seen in his epic design for the Fagus-Werk, a factory built in 1911 in the town of Alfed an der Leine.
